answer: Each identity is gated by a Wesolowski VDF: producing its output requires a continuous chain of sequential modular squarings, while the compact proof is checked efficiently. GPUs cannot parallelize one chain to erase its elapsed-time cost; they can run separate clone chains in parallel, but each clone incurs that cost. This trellis of per-identity delays makes mass Sybil creation costly, not impossible, and avoids a hollow claim of absolute GPU resistance; a plume of parallel hardware still faces the sequential bottleneck per identity.
